technique_why: A misty wood is a classic paint-along: a wet blended haze first, then soft far shapes, then the pale birches and gold leaves built up in dabs and dashes over it, all with a few brushes and repeated marks a beginner can make.
subject: A misty autumn birch grove with a leaf-covered path running back into the fog
focal_point: The two big leaning birches left of center and the path fading into the fog between them and the right-hand birches
light: A hazy low sun at the upper left, glowing through the mist; trunks and leaves are lit on their left sides
why: The fog is one wet blend over the whole canvas, so the beginner gets the mood down first and everything after sits in it. Then the far wood, floor, path and faint far birches, still soft and cool, then the gold undergrowth and the leaf carpet, so the big birches go on last over a finished ground and stay the sharpest, highest-contrast things in the picture. The hanging leaves and the palest lights come at the very end, in front of everything.

things.name: The misty glow
things.why: The fog behind the grove is one soft gradient, gold at the sun and blue-gray across the rest, blended wet in one go.

things.name: The dark wood on the right
things.why: A far tree line seen as a soft mass: a dark base, then a lighter misty edge, with no leaf detail.
things.plain: the plain dark blue-green wood shape

things.name: The leafy forest floor
things.why: Ground laid as a base lighter at the back and darker in front, then textured in passes; it lacks a leaf mark, so the leaves are its horizontal-stroke texture passes, darkest first.

things.name: The path into the fog
things.why: The path is flat ground laid in horizontal strokes and textured with the same leaf dashes; the element lacks a path that narrows to a point, so the step says to narrow it toward the fog.

things.name: The far birches in the mist
things.called: the thin pale birch trunks in the mist
things.why: Thin white trunks with bark marks, kept pale and soft because they are far away; no shading or light step.
things.plain: the plain pale blue-white far trunks

things.name: The golden undergrowth
things.why: Bushes are leaves in a mass: dark dabs, then gold dabs, then a few pale taps on the lit side.
things.plain: the plain ochre and olive bush shapes

things.name: The mossy boulder
things.why: A rounded rock with a mossy lit top: a gray shape built from an oval, then the light on top.
things.left_out: the rock's own shadow side and texture; it stays two values

things.name: The big birches
things.called: the five big white birch trunks in front
things.why: The focal trees: pale trunk, shade on the side away from the light, broken dark bark marks, then light on the lit side.
things.plain: the plain pale gray-white trunk shapes
things.left_out: the fine branches and twigs; the trunks run off the top edge instead

things.name: The hanging gold leaves
things.called: the gold leaves hanging at the top
things.why: Leaves in loose clusters across the top: gold dabs, then a few pale taps on the lit side.

steps.name: Blend the misty glow

lays.what: the whole canvas: a pale gold glow at the upper left, pale haze blue across the middle, deeper haze blue down the right side, all the way to the bottom edge

steps.after: The whole canvas is a soft misty blend, gold glowing at the upper left, pale blue-gray in the middle and deeper blue on the right, running to every edge. No trees, ground or leaves yet.
steps.why: The fog sits behind everything, so it goes on first, straight through where the trees and ground will go.

steps.name: Dab the dark wood on the right

lays.what: a soft dark blue-green mass of far trees down the right half, from near the top to the middle of the canvas, with ragged tops

steps.after: A soft dark blue-green wood fills the right side down to the middle, its ragged top fading into the blue fog. The left half is still the misty blend, and the lower half has no ground yet.

steps.name: Mist the wood's left edge

lays.what: a lighter misty blue-green dry-brushed along the left edge and the bottom of the dark wood, where it fades into the fog

steps.after: The dark wood now fades into the fog on its left side and at the bottom, darkest at the far right. Still no ground, trunks or leaves.

steps.name: Lay in the forest floor

lays.what: the whole lower third: warm ochre at the back by the fog, blending to rust brown along the bottom edge

steps.after: The lower third is a smooth floor, warm ochre at the back and rust brown at the bottom, with no leaf marks or path yet. The fog and the dark wood stand above it.

steps.name: Lay the path into the fog

lays.what: a mauve-brown path from the bottom center, wide in front and narrowing back to a thin strip that disappears into the fog just right of the middle

steps.after: A plain mauve-brown path runs from the bottom center back into the fog, wide in front and thin at the back, on the flat ochre-and-rust floor. No leaves on it yet.

steps.name: Pull the thin far birches

lays.what: thin pale blue-white trunks: one just left of the path, two in front of the dark wood right of the path, and a few faint ghost trunks in the haze at the far left, each tapering up off the top

steps.after: Thin pale trunks stand in the fog, one left of the path, two against the dark wood and a few faint ones at the left, all plain with no marks. No bushes or big trees yet.

steps.name: Mark the far bark softly

lays.what: small soft gray bark marks across the thin trunks, a few on each, fewer on the faint left ones

steps.after: The thin far birches carry soft gray bark marks, still pale and low in contrast. The floor and path are still plain.

steps.name: Dab the dark of the undergrowth

lays.what: ochre dabs in a bank of bushes across the left half from the edge to the path, and olive dabs in a low band at the foot of the dark wood on the right, over the bases of the far trunks

steps.after: A dabbed bank of ochre bushes fills the left half down to the floor, and a low olive band sits under the dark wood on the right. No bright gold leaves yet.

steps.name: Dab gold on the bushes

lays.what: bright gold dabs over most of the left bushes, thickest on the upper left facing the light, with the ochre showing between

steps.after: The left bushes glow gold with ochre showing in the gaps and lower down; the olive band on the right stays dull. The rock and leaf carpet aren't there yet.

steps.name: Build the boulder

lays.what: the whole boulder right of the path as one flat gray-violet shape, built from a low oval and a curved piece on each side

steps.after: A flat gray-violet boulder sits right of the path in front of the olive band, with no moss on it.

steps.name: Lay the moss on the boulder

lays.what: olive moss on the top and left of the boulder, in curved strokes following its round top, gray left showing on the right and bottom

steps.after: The boulder has a mossy olive top and left side, gray on the right and at the bottom. The floor still has no leaf marks.

steps.name: Dash the dark fallen leaves

lays.what: short rust-brown horizontal dashes across the floor, bigger and closer at the bottom, smaller toward the fog
a few rust dashes scattered on the path, more in front

steps.after: The floor and the front of the path are covered in short rust leaf dashes, larger near the bottom; the far floor stays smoother. No gold leaves on the ground yet.

steps.name: Dash the ochre fallen leaves

lays.what: warm ochre horizontal dashes over the rust ones, leaving rust showing between
ochre dashes along the path's edges and middle, the mauve showing between

steps.after: The leaf carpet now mixes ochre and rust dashes, and the path is strewn with leaves with mauve showing between. The big birches aren't there yet.

steps.name: Pull the big birch trunks

lays.what: five big pale trunks: a thin one at the far left, the two big leaning ones left of center, and two straight ones on the right, each widest at the floor and tapering up off the top edge

steps.after: Five plain pale gray-white trunks stand over the leaf carpet and bushes, two leaning left of center, with no shading or bark marks.

steps.name: Shade the right side of the trunks

lays.what: gray violet dry-brushed down the right side of each trunk, darker toward the base

steps.after: Each trunk is pale on the left and gray-violet on its right side, darker near the floor. Still no bark marks.

steps.name: Add the dark bark marks

lays.what: broken near-black marks across each trunk, many reaching only partway, more and bigger toward the base, and the dark at each trunk's foot

steps.after: The big trunks carry broken charcoal bark marks, heavy at the feet and sparse higher up. The left edges are not yet lit.

steps.name: Catch the light on the bark

lays.what: cream dry-brushed down the left side of each trunk, over the dry marks in places

steps.after: The trunks glow cream on the left, gray on the right, with dark marks between. No hanging leaves at the top yet.

stages.name: The hanging leaves and last lights

steps.name: Dab the hanging gold leaves

lays.what: loose clusters of gold and ochre leaves across the top: thick in the upper left glow, a scattered spray through the top middle, and a cluster at the upper right, over the trunks in places

steps.after: Gold leaves hang across the top, thickest at the upper left and crossing the trunks in places, with no pale tips yet.

steps.name: Tap the palest leaves

lays.what: a few pale lemon taps on the left side of the leaf clusters
a few pale lemon taps on the tops of the left bushes facing the light

steps.after: The hanging leaves and the left bushes catch a few pale lemon lights on their lit sides; the floor leaves are still ochre and rust.

steps.name: Dash the sunlit fallen leaves

lays.what: a few pale lemon dashes on the floor in front and between the trunks
a few pale lemon dashes down the middle of the path

steps.after: A scatter of pale lemon leaves lights the floor and the path. The painting is finished.
steps.unit: The sunlit leaves on the floor
